::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What this lesson is for

Until now you have looked at your **whole** table. But usually you want just a part of it — only your
landing site, only the big catches, or only a few columns.

This lesson gives you three simple commands to do that: **list the values** in a column, **keep only the
rows** you want, and **keep only the columns** you want. Press **Run** on each box. Remember: **you
cannot break anything.**
:::

These commands come from a free toolkit called **dplyr**. Run the box below once to switch it on (the
first time, it may take a few moments to download) — it also loads the small example table from the last
lesson.

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

example <- data.frame(
  trip_id      = c("trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_2", "trip_2"),
  landing_date = c("2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-06", "2024-01-06"),
  site         = c("Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Vanga", "Vanga"),
  gear         = c("hand line", "hand line", "hand line", "gillnet", "gillnet"),
  fish         = c("Tilapia", "Snapper", "Octopus", "Tilapia", "Snapper"),
  catch_kg     = c(12, 5, 3, 8, 6)
)
example
```

## What values are in a column?

Before you can ask for "only Vanga", you need to know which sites exist. **`distinct()`** lists each
value in a column **once**, leaving out the repeats. Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
distinct(example, site)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**What you should see:** just **Shimoni** and **Vanga**. Even though Shimoni is on three rows, it is
listed once. This is also how you find the **exact spelling** of a value to use in the next step.
:::

Now on your own data — these are your real landing sites. Press **Run**, then try changing `gaul_2_name`
to `gear` to see your fishing methods:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
distinct(landings, gaul_2_name)
```

## Show only the rows you want

**`filter()`** keeps only the rows that match a condition you give — for example, only the `gillnet`
trips.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Two small things to get right:

- Use **two** equals signs `==` for "is equal to" (one `=` means something else and will not work).
- A word like `"gillnet"` needs **quotes**. A number, like `5`, does not.
:::

Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
filter(example, gear == "gillnet")
```

```{=html}
<style>
tr.keep td { background:#e6f4ea !important; }
tr.drop td { color:#b0b0b0 !important; }
</style>
<table class="table" style="font-size:.9rem">
  <thead><tr><th>site</th><th>gear</th><th>fish</th><th>catch_kg</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr class="drop"><td>Shimoni</td><td>hand line</td><td>Tilapia</td><td>12</td></tr>
    <tr class="drop"><td>Shimoni</td><td>hand line</td><td>Snapper</td><td>5</td></tr>
    <tr class="drop"><td>Shimoni</td><td>hand line</td><td>Octopus</td><td>3</td></tr>
    <tr class="keep"><td>Vanga</td><td>gillnet</td><td>Tilapia</td><td>8</td></tr>
    <tr class="keep"><td>Vanga</td><td>gillnet</td><td>Snapper</td><td>6</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
*`filter(gear == "gillnet")` keeps the green rows and drops the rest.*

You can also filter on a **number** — no quotes needed. This keeps only catches heavier than 5 kg:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
filter(example, catch_kg > 5)
```

On your real data, keep only one site (use a name you saw with `distinct` above). Press **Run**, then
change the name to one of **your** sites:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
filter(landings, gaul_2_name == "Vanga")
```

## Keep only the columns you want

Your table has many columns. Often you want just a few — say the date, the site and the weight.
**`select()`** keeps only the columns you name:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
select(example, landing_date, site, catch_kg)
```

```{=html}
<style>
.cols span { display:inline-block; padding:3px 8px; margin:2px; border-radius:5px; font-family:monospace; font-size:.85rem; }
.cols .keep { background:#e6f4ea; border:1px solid #8cc6a0; }
.cols .drop { background:#f2f2f2; color:#aaa; border:1px solid #ddd; }
</style>
<div class="cols">
  Keep: <span class="keep">landing_date</span><span class="keep">site</span><span class="keep">catch_kg</span>
  &#160;&#160; Drop: <span class="drop">trip_id</span><span class="drop">gear</span><span class="drop">fish</span>
</div>
```
*`select()` keeps the green columns and leaves out the rest.*

On your real data, keep just three useful columns. Press **Run**, then try adding another column name:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
select(landings, landing_date, gaul_2_name, catch_kg)
```

## Do two steps at once: the pipe `|>`

Most real questions need two steps: keep only **your** site, **and** keep only a few columns. The little
symbol **`|>`** (called the *pipe*) lets you do steps **in order**, left to right. Read it as the word
**"then"**.

The box below says: *take the landings, **then** keep only Vanga, **then** keep these three columns.*
Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
landings |>
  filter(gaul_2_name == "Vanga") |>
  select(landing_date, gear, catch_kg)
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
This is the kind of question you will ask most often: **narrow the rows, then narrow the columns.** Change
`"Vanga"` to one of your own sites and press **Run** again.
:::

## What you have learned

- **`distinct(table, column)`** — list the values in a column once (find your sites, gears, …).
- **`filter(table, condition)`** — keep only the rows that match (use `==`, and quotes for words).
- **`select(table, columns…)`** — keep only the columns you name.
- **`|>`** ("then") — do several steps in order.

Next: **Add it up** — totals and averages by site, gear or month.
